issue.title: Real-Obsidian e2e trust step leaves Obsidian's Settings window active, so modals mount invisibly and keys reach the editor

task_type_fields.impact: Real-Obsidian runners that open a Modal after the trust click get invisible modals and keys that go to the editor, which looks like product focus or dispatch bugs. This may explain undiagnosed real-key failures such as bob-cli-nq and bob-cli-nr.
task_type_fields.location: bob-plugins scripts/obsidian-record-card-e2e.cjs trustCommunityPlugins (and the runners that copy or import it)
task_type_fields.repro:
Proposed by bob-cli-om.10 (note #2, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP), triaged by bob-cli-om.land.

`trustCommunityPlugins` (bob-plugins `scripts/obsidian-record-card-e2e.cjs:661`, copied or imported by obsidian-intention-card-e2e, obsidian-projects-ui-e2e, obsidian-title-block-e2e, obsidian-title-slot-spike, and obsidian-prose-field-e2e) clicks "Trust author and enable plugins". In Obsidian 1.15 that opens Settings as a separate window, which becomes `window.activeWindow`. Under Xvfb nothing refocuses the vault window, so every `Modal` afterwards mounts in the Settings document: it reports "open" but is invisible, and trusted CDP keys go to the editor.

Repro: on athena (Obsidian 1.15.1, Xvfb), run `xvfb-run -a node scripts/obsidian-record-card-e2e.cjs -e /snap/obsidian/current/app/obsidian` (TMPDIR=/tmp/<short>; see bob-cli-np) on a fresh profile that still needs the trust click. After trust, evaluate `window.activeWindow === window`; it is false while the Settings window is open.

om.10 fixed only `scripts/obsidian-prose-field-e2e.cjs` (around lines 300-395): it finds the Settings CDP target, closes it, and dispatches a main-window focus, checking `window.activeWindow === window && window.activeDocument === document`. Fold that into the shared trust step so every runner gets it.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-om.10 found and fixed this focus trap only in the prose-field runner; the shared trust helper used by the other real-Obsidian runners still has it.

payload.entry: Related diagnostic from bob-cli-pl.4.1.3 note #1: its home-card runner imports trustCommunityPlugins from obsidian-record-card-e2e.cjs, which still returns immediately after trust.click() without asserting main-window focus. Phase saw no Task Card on both an untyped control and a ^prj note. This is a candidate explanation, not a confirmed reproduction of ox; no +1 or new duplicate filed. Home-card landing repair will validate activeWindow/activeDocument before restoring the omitted Task Card acceptance.

evidence.note: In the Mail Close scratch-vault run on macOS Obsidian 1.14.4, the trust prompt opened a separate about:blank Settings target; window.activeWindow === window and window.activeDocument === document were both false, so the card mounted invisibly. Closing that Settings CDP target, activating the vault target, and restoring focus made the card visible; all four screenshots then captured. This independently reproduces the shared trust-helper focus failure.
